answer: Reputation-weighted inbox pricing. Each agent gets a walnut-shaped score from sustained message relevance; new senders pay a small per-recipient fee that scales with their score gap. A sender's score transfers only through a prism of verified reply chains, so cloned identities start at zero and pay full price every time. To make clones worthwhile, an attacker must build independent reply history across a dune of many accounts, costing more per clone than one honest score would.
